review_role: Independent source, coverage and question-key scope challenge; no summary or reader/grade outputs inspected
scope: Mayfair 2010/2013 English 2–4-player base; previous-Mayfair unified base clarifications only. No expansions or optional Gamble Variant.
key_accuracy_verdict: All 31 intended base rulings are supported; minor completeness and wording issues identified. No expansion rule is needed for the current questions.
scope_verdict: Answer-key and scope-map required/background classifications disagree for Q05, Q09, Q15, Q22. Q08 still imposes an unasked trading fact; Q03 and Q20 contain narrower unasked background clauses. No global authority-gap scoring cap is justified.
summary_findings: No substantive wrong action cost, wager calculation, scoring example, takeover value, eligibility or boss-tie result found.
At least one material timing exception is missing: no initiating trades after End of Game draw. Two smaller unasked base rules are initial chip/piece setup and number of participants in a trade.
Do not equate an entire source heading or contextual key fact with independently asked coverage.

per_question.question: How are starting properties and money assigned, where do the dealt cards go, and how is the End of Game card inserted?
per_question.finding: Starting properties, money, visible initial discards and deck insertion are correctly asked and answered. This does not ask initial component selection, banker selection, or initial scoring-chip placement.
per_question.source: Original p2 Setting Up; unified p5

per_question.question: Who takes the first turn, how does turn order proceed, and what is the normal Draw/Play sequence?
per_question.finding: First roller, leftward succession and Draw-before-Play order match the original two-step base sequence. Expansion draw/action steps are correctly excluded.
per_question.source: Original p2 Taking Turns/On Every Turn; p3 Ending Step 1

per_question.question: You draw the card for an empty lot. When is it acquired and paid, and do the printed card starting-money values pay again?
per_question.finding: The new lot is marked before payout, earns $1 immediately, and card starting money is setup-only. Requiring payment to every OTHER marked lot goes beyond the singular lot acquisition/payment question; retain new-lot payment as required and classify all-other-lot payout as background here (it is asked elsewhere).
per_question.source: Original p2 Setting Up/Take Over Your Lot/Owned Lots Pay

per_question.question: You draw a lot card for a sprawled tile with an opponent’s 5, although the board prints 2. What happens to the tile and die, and who receives its imminent matching-color money?
per_question.finding: Replacing an opposing die preserves current 5, not printed 2; tile remains and takeover precedes the stated matching payout. No additional unprovided casino dice or ties should be invented.
per_question.source: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid

per_question.question: When do same-color tiles form one casino, can they be divided, and is the boss determined by total pips or something else?
per_question.finding: Core casino geometry, indivisibility and highest individual die are accurate. Scope map correctly makes casino/player color independence background, but answer-key required_facts still requires it. Harmonize the key with the scope map; do not score that unasked fact.
per_question.source: Original p1 Casino Tiles/Player Dice; p2 Who Owns What

per_question.question: A three-tile gold casino contains Red 5 and Blue 3 and 2; Red also owns two marked lots. On a gold payout, how much money and how many points does each receive from these holdings?
per_question.finding: Red $7 and three awarded casino points; Blue $5 and no casino points. These are awards, not an unspecified scoring-track destination.
per_question.source: Original p2 Owned Lots Pay/Money Paid/Points Earned

per_question.question: How does Pay The Strip differ from a color payout, and what qualifies a casino whose only one tile touches The Strip?
per_question.finding: Color pays everywhere; one edge touching Strip qualifies the complete casino. Money/points cover all its tiles.
per_question.source: Original p2 Pay Based on Color/Pay The Strip; unified p8

per_question.question: Which actions may you take in Play, in what order and how often, and may another player perform an action on your turn?
per_question.finding: Five base actions, any order, repeatability, reorganization restriction and no off-turn action are responsive. The appended requirement that trading may occur at any time is unasked: trading is not an action (unified p9), and the question asks actions. Move it to contextual background in BOTH files. Q17 directly asks trading timing.
per_question.source: Original p3 Step 2 Play/Reorganize; p4 Trading

per_question.question: How do you build on your marked lot whose board price is $6 and printed die is 2? State cost, marker and die handling, and tile choice.
per_question.finding: $6, reclaim marker, available tile choice and own die 2 are correct. Scope map correctly backgrounds automatic neighbor merging because no neighbor or merger is asked; answer-key still lists that as required. Harmonize.
per_question.source: Original p3 Build; unified p10 Build

per_question.question: You boss a gold casino and want to sprawl onto an edge-adjacent empty unowned $9 lot with printed die 3. What do you pay and place, and may you instead sprawl onto an opponent’s marked lot or a merely diagonal lot?
per_question.finding: $18, available gold tile, own die 3, boss origin and empty unowned edge-adjacent target conditions are correct. Given actor/target conditions are preserved.
per_question.source: Original p3 Sprawl

per_question.question: How does remodeling a two-tile casino work, including eligibility, cost, tile supply, and a merger with a neighboring casino whose highest die beats yours?
per_question.finding: Boss-only whole-casino recolor, $10 cost, enough replacement tiles, unchanged dice and new neighboring higher boss are correct. Because the question explicitly asks how remodeling works including tile supply, state that replaced old tiles return to the tile stacks (unified p11); this matters to subsequent available supply, and should not be left implicit in exchange wording.
per_question.source: Original p3 Remodel and example; unified p11

per_question.question: May a non-boss with one die reorganize a casino with dice 5, 3 and 2? State who pays how much, which dice roll and who rolls them, and where multiple dice may return.
per_question.finding: Acting non-boss with a die pays all ten pips; every owner rerolls own dice and may assign only among their own original tiles.
per_question.source: Original p3 Reorganize

per_question.question: A die was reorganized earlier this turn and its casino then merges into a larger casino. Can the larger casino be reorganized this turn, and are free boss-tie rerolls prohibited too?
per_question.finding: Any already-reorganized die blocks reorganization of the merged casino this turn; free boss disputes are a separate reroll procedure.
per_question.source: Original p3 Reorganize; p4 Reroll if Tied; unified p11

per_question.question: After a merger, Red 5 and Blue 5 tie above Green 4. What rerolls, at what cost, and who bosses if both 5s reroll to 3? What if all largest tied dice belong to one player, or only smaller dice tie?
per_question.finding: Correct free current-highest-only rerolls; unchanged Green 4 wins over new 3s, same-player high ties and lower ties do not reroll. Iteration is correctly until one PLAYER owns highest, permitting multiple equal dice of that player.
per_question.source: Original p4 After Each Action Reroll if Tied and diagram

per_question.question: You have $18 and gamble at an opponent’s four-tile casino whose boss has $15. What is the maximum bet, who gets the House card, and how many times may you gamble this turn?
per_question.finding: Maximum $15, House card to boss, once per own turn are correct. Opponent-boss eligibility is given in this scenario; scope map correctly backgrounds it, whereas answer-key includes must choose another player casino in required_facts. Harmonize.
per_question.source: Original p4 Gamble

per_question.question: For a legal $4 bet against a boss who has $7, resolve every possible two-dice sum group, including the limited doubled payout. Is a winning bettor also losing their stake?
per_question.finding: All sums partition correctly: 3/4/9/10/11 gain $4, 2/12 gain only available $7, 5/6/7/8 lose $4. Winning stake is retained/returned, not an additional loss. No layoff variant imported.
per_question.source: Original p4 Gamble; unified p13

per_question.question: What may be traded, when may trading occur, how are traded lots and dice transferred, and what cannot be promised or traded?
per_question.finding: Base tradable assets, timing, same-current-pip replacements, forbidden points/tiles/future-turn promises and no off-turn actions are correct. The prompt does not explicitly ask whether a trade may involve more than two players.
per_question.source: Original p4 Trading

per_question.question: Starting at score 8, where do single casino awards of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 points leave you? Can two separate one-tile casinos combine their awards, and in what order are different casinos scored?
per_question.finding: All numeric destinations exactly match original example. Separate casino awards cannot pool; score smallest first, choice on equal sizes. A new numeric example would add no rule.
per_question.source: Original p2 Scoring; p3 scoring example and multiple casinos

per_question.question: What happens when the End of Game card is drawn, including remaining actions, final payouts, winner and tied score? Is there an immediate alternative win condition?
per_question.finding: Immediate ending, no subsequent Play, final lot/Strip payouts, point then money tiebreak and immediate base 90+ win are correct. The prompt asks remaining actions, but does not ask whether a trade may begin after the end card. Ledger cannot count no-initiated-trades coverage here.
per_question.source: Original p4 Winning; unified p16

per_question.question: In two-player play, what happens to F cards drawn during setup and during a turn? May anyone build on F, and can a turn pay more than once before actions?
per_question.finding: No F construction, setup discard-and-replace, F-turn payments/discard/repeat and multiple payouts are correct and positively applicable previous-Mayfair base text. End of Game still ends immediately is true but no End of Game interruption is asked; put this background clause outside required facts. Do not import the excluded revised setup treatment.
per_question.source: Original p4 2-Player Rules/Winning; unified p16 2-Player Rules

per_question.question: All nine gold tiles are on the board. Can you build another gold tile using the spare tenth tile, sprawl a gold casino, or remodel a three-tile casino to gold? May you build a different available color?
per_question.finding: Nine usable tiles per color, spare tenth replacement only; all three gold placement routes unavailable, another available color can be built on own lot.
per_question.source: Original p1 Casino Tiles; p3 Available Tiles/Build/Sprawl/Remodel

per_question.question: All twelve of your dice are on the board when you build, sprawl or inherit a sprawled tile. How do you place the required die, what happens to the vacated tile and its scoring, and what if it was the casino’s only die?
per_question.finding: Move existing ownership die, keep vacated tile ownerless but counting toward casino size; last die removal leaves no owner/boss. Scope correctly backgrounds trade-to-free-die; answer-key incorrectly keeps it required. Harmonize. No owner means nobody receives that casino’s boss points until it again has a boss.
per_question.source: Original p3 Available Dice; unified p6 Available Dice

per_question.question: A property draw claims a sprawled casino tile with no die; the board prints 2, while the die removed from it used to be 5. What die do you place, does the tile change, and when does its matching casino pay?
per_question.finding: Empty-die takeover resets to printed 2, tile remains, acquisition precedes payout and die earns $2 in the stated matching payment.
per_question.source: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid; unified p7

per_question.question: You draw the card for your own sprawled tile, whose die is now 6 although the board prints 2. Does ownership or value change, and what does that die earn if its casino pays?
per_question.finding: Unified p7 explicitly leaves existing own die alone: ownership unchanged, value 6 and income $6.
per_question.source: Unified p7 Step 2; original p2 Money Paid

per_question.question: All ten of your markers are on lots and you acquire another empty lot. How is ownership marked, what happens to the vacated lot, and which of the two lots receives the coming owned-lot payout?
per_question.finding: Unified p6 marker-exhaustion rule applies to gaining a base lot: relocate marker, lose old lot, newly marked lot receives imminent $1.
per_question.source: Unified p6 Available Player Markers; original p2 Draw/Owned Lots Pay

per_question.question: May a player conceal money or piece counts, forbid inspection of a discard pile, or deny a bank payout because the physical bank is empty?
per_question.finding: Public money/component counts/discards and unlimited bank are base resource clarifications. No Underworld held-card rule is needed to answer.
per_question.source: Original p1 Money; unified p6 Your Resources/Available Money

per_question.question: A casino has two Red 6s and a Blue 3. During a trade one Red 6 is replaced by Green’s die. What value does Green’s die have, must anything reroll before further trades or actions, and who rolls?
per_question.finding: Trade preserves 6, creating Red/Green highest tie; owners reroll their tied dice free and immediately, excluding Blue 3, before further initiated trades/actions.
per_question.source: Original p4 Trading/Reroll if Tied; unified p9 Settling Who’s the Boss

per_question.question: You draw a card and replace one of Red’s tied highest 5s in a casino with your own 5; another Red 5 remains. Is the boss tie postponed until after payment or Play, and does this reroll count as a paid reorganization?
per_question.finding: Immediate takeover tie resolves before payments; current highest rerolls free and not as paid reorganization. Unified p9 applies expressly to taking over sprawled spaces, with no expansion dependency.
per_question.source: Unified p7 Step 2/p9 Settling Who’s the Boss; p11 Reorganize

per_question.question: May you reorganize a casino where you alone own all dice, or one where you own none? Does reorganizing only one of your dice avoid paying for the opponents’ pips?
per_question.finding: Sole owner is eligible, no-own-die player is not, and selection of just one die cannot reduce all-dice reorganization cost.
per_question.source: Original p3 Reorganize; unified p11

per_question.question: All twelve of your ownership dice are on casino tiles. Must you remove a tile’s die just to gamble, and may you gamble at your own casino if no opponent bosses any casino?
per_question.finding: Any dice may make gambling rolls without vacating ownership; opposing boss is required and absent legal house means no gamble.
per_question.source: Unified p6 Available Dice; p13 Gamble

per_question.question: On your turn you trade for an opponent’s die so that you can reorganize their casino, then promise to pay them for a sprawl only if the reorganization gives you control. If the reroll does not make you boss so the agreed sprawl cannot happen, do the subsequent steps of the trade proceed? Could the opponent instead perform the sprawl on your turn?
per_question.finding: Interrupted subsequent trade steps stop, sprawl requires acting player to boss, and opponent cannot act off-turn. All are valid base paragraphs. Wording pay them for a sprawl leaves the intended sprawl actor somewhat unclear; name the acting player as performer when editing. Interpret the conditional promised steps as THIS turn, not prohibited future-turn promises.
per_question.source: Unified p15 Trading; original p3 Sprawl/p4 Trading

all_core_passage_coverage_challenge.passage: Unified p16 two-player setup and final no actions/trades
all_core_passage_coverage_challenge.detail: Q20 asks two-player setup and Q19 asks no remaining actions. No actual question clause asks whether a trade may be initiated when End of Game is drawn.

proposed_additions.question: The End of Game card has just been drawn. Before the final payout, may players initiate a last-minute trade of money or a casino die, perhaps to change who wins a tied score?
proposed_additions.answer: No. The game ends immediately when that card is drawn, and players may not initiate trades then. Resolve the final owned-lot and Strip payouts, then compare points and use money to break a points tie.
proposed_additions.source: Original p4 Winning; unified physical p16 Winning, first paragraph (no actions or initiated trades on End of Game draw).
proposed_additions.novelty: Previously unasked timing exception: Q17 permits trading at any time, while Q19 only asks remaining actions. No question asks end-card priority over initiating a trade. The ledger claims this coverage without an actual asked clause.

proposed_additions.question: During setup, which pieces does each player take, and where is each player’s scoring chip placed before the first turn?
proposed_additions.answer: Each player takes an action card and the scoring chip, markers and dice of one player color. Place every player’s scoring chip on 0 on the scoring track.
proposed_additions.source: Original p2 Setting Up, first and third paragraphs; unified physical p5 Setting Up.
proposed_additions.novelty: Previously unasked setup rules. Q01 is specifically about starting properties, starting money, dealt cards and End of Game insertion; neither it nor another question asks initial chip score or matching player pieces.

proposed_additions.question: Must a trade be between exactly two players, or may three players participate in one agreed trade of their money, lots and casino dice?
proposed_additions.answer: Any number of players may be involved in a trade, so a three-player trade is permitted, subject to the ordinary restrictions on traded assets and timing.
proposed_additions.source: Unified physical p15 At Any Time: Trading, first paragraph: any number of players may be involved. Original p4 Trading supplies base assets and restrictions.
proposed_additions.novelty: Previously unasked actor rule, positively applicable to base trading. Q17 asks what/when/how transfer, and Q31 asks interruption; neither asks permitted number of participants. No card effects or expansion assets are used.

rejected_candidates.reason: This fact is only contextual in Q05, so it cannot be claimed as directly tested there. However Q09 expressly asks tile choice and its required answer permits any available color; a separate standalone question adds little operational coverage and is not needed for saturation of meaningful rulings.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Build then reorganize, remodel then sprawl, or a returned-tile build example
rejected_candidates.reason: These are mechanical combinations of order, eligibility and supply already asked. Fix Q11 old-tile return wording rather than create a separate action-combination question.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Who breaks a tie in the first-turn two-dice roll, or a game tie in both points and money?
rejected_candidates.reason: Supplied applicable base paragraphs do not state the resolution. Do not invent an authority rule or impose a global scoring cap.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A new rule to settle two-player setup F cards by setting aside then reshuffling
rejected_candidates.reason: Excluded revised edition; supplied previous-Mayfair base p16 says discard and draw a replacement.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Acquire/raise, Underworld points/card actions, risers, expansion special effects, or optional laying off
rejected_candidates.reason: Excluded modules and optional variant. Unified p2 explicitly instructs ignoring rules for absent expansion elements.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Choose a banker as a standalone new question
rejected_candidates.reason: Unasked administrative setup direction, but does not produce a distinctive rules ruling; the proposed setup addition focuses on player pieces and the actual initial score state.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Trade at any time as a new question
rejected_candidates.reason: Already explicitly asked by Q17; removing it from Q08 required facts repairs grading scope, not missing bank coverage.

source_applicability.baseline: Mayfair copyright 2010/2013 English base rules, four printed pages
source_applicability.unified_applicability: Physical p2 explicitly says ignore rules applying to absent Up!/Underworld elements. Base-only resource, own-sprawl takeover, immediate boss disputes, reorganization, gambling stake/any-dice, trading and two-player setup clarifications have no dependency on those elements.
source_applicability.excluded: No risers/raise, acquire/Underworld cards, revised 2024 six-player setup, Americana, Con Jobs, or optional Gamble Variant imported.
native_image_inspection: Original original-rulebook-p2.png viewed directly; setup deck diagram and payout diagram confirm extracted procedure. No contradictory diagram found.

delivery_receipt.method: Every six permitted text inputs was printed with exact content in contiguous <=4800-character chunks, with path/start/end/total/SHA256, one chunk per tool result. Each command requested max_output_tokens=5000 (>=4000). Each returned exit 0 without truncation. This records actual model-visible delivery, not merely filesystem loading.
